records.name: YARA-X
records.description: Rust-based rule-scanning engine with CLI and language bindings; check its documented differences before migrating YARA rules.
records.task: Rule scanning and migration from YARA
records.incremental_value: An independently usable successor engine, rather than only a mention in the existing YARA description.
records.constraints: Most rules can be migrated, but regex, modules, and APIs have documented differences. The smoke check confirms rejection of an unescaped opening brace. BSD-3-Clause.
records.next_check: Add a paired YARA/YARA-X compatible-rule and incompatible-rule fixture.
records.reproduced_scope: Python API positive/negative matching and strict-regex CompileError

records.name: CyberChef
records.description: Browser-based workbench for decoding, decompressing, and transforming data with exportable recipes.
records.incremental_value: A data-transformation workbench between file identification and deeper analysis; exported recipes can become evidence artifacts.
records.constraints: Browser use and building from source have different prerequisites. The reviewed source-build instructions require Node 24. Apache-2.0.
records.next_check: Pin a build and verify an exported recipe against self-authored encoded/compressed input.

records.name: Scapy
records.description: Python packet framework for dissecting and constructing protocols, reading PCAPs, and scripting network experiments.
records.task: Programmatic protocol parsing and packet construction
records.incremental_value: Complements Wireshark inspection and HTTP proxies with repeatable parser/builder experiments and offline PCAP handling.
records.constraints: Offline parsing differs from live capture or transmission, which have host, permission, and driver requirements. GPL-2.0.
records.next_check: Add a self-authored custom protocol layer and PCAP fixture; the completed smoke test was offline only.
records.reproduced_scope: Offline packet/PCAP round trip and independent IP/UDP checksums; no traffic sent

records.name: Construct
records.description: Declarative Python library for parsing and building binary formats with composable schemas and validation.
records.incremental_value: Complements Kaitai with composable Python parsing and building, useful for checking field hypotheses and reconstructing files.
records.constraints: Schemas must correctly model lengths, context, and validation. GitHub reports NOASSERTION, but the reviewed LICENSE contains MIT terms.
records.next_check: Reuse a small format fixture for independent golden bytes and a Construct/Kaitai comparison.
records.reproduced_scope: Golden bytes, parse/build, wrong magic, truncation, trailing-data rejection

records.name: Vineflower
records.description: Java decompiler focused on modern language features and readable output; requires Java 17 or newer to run current releases.
records.incremental_value: Adds a standalone JVM decompiler beside the existing Android DEX and managed-code workbenches.
records.constraints: Current releases require Java 17+ to run; host requirements and target class versions are separate. Obfuscation and other Java versions were not tested. Apache-2.0.
records.next_check: Publish the bounded Java 17 record/switch-expression rebuild case, then extend the target-version matrix.
records.reproduced_scope: Java 17 record/switch expression, rebuild, main output and five branch vectors

records.name: ghidriff
records.description: Ghidra-based command-line binary diffing engine with JSON, Markdown, and optional HTML reports; requires compatible Ghidra, PyGhidra, and JDK versions.
records.incremental_value: Adds CLI automation and JSON/Markdown/optional HTML reports to the existing pairwise diffing tools.
records.constraints: Ghidra, PyGhidra/JPype, and the matching JDK must be pinned. The reviewed development target is Ghidra 12.0.4 with PyGhidra 3.x; older examples do not prove broad compatibility. GPL-3.0.
records.next_check: Diff self-built v1/v2 binaries with known added, removed, and changed functions, checking both JSON and Markdown.

records.name: oletools
records.description: Python tools for inspecting Office, OLE, and RTF files and extracting macros, embedded objects, and other document artifacts.
records.incremental_value: Fills the document-input gap: macro extraction, embedded objects, and related document artifacts rather than predominantly PE inputs.
records.constraints: Coverage varies by subtool; XLM workflows have optional dependencies. README news mentions 0.60.3 while the latest GitHub release endpoint returns 0.60.2. Own code uses BSD-style terms, with MIT/third-party exceptions.
records.next_check: Pin the actual distribution version and verify extraction from a self-authored document.

records.name: AssetRipper
records.description: Unity asset-analysis and export tool with version-dependent support and additional paid Premium features.
records.incremental_value: Complements Cpp2IL/Il2CppDumper code and metadata analysis with asset inspection and export.
records.constraints: The README claims Unity 3.5.0–6000.4.X, with varying support quality. The GPL-3.0 base and paid Premium features must be distinguished.
records.next_check: Export a self-built Unity project and compare assets and references against the original.

records.name: Speakeasy
records.description: Windows emulation framework for PE files, drivers, and shellcode that produces API reports within a modeled runtime.
records.task: Modeled Windows execution and API reports
records.incremental_value: A smaller emulation/reporting path beside full sandbox VMs.
records.constraints: API, filesystem, registry, and runtime behavior are modeled. Signature-only stubs can report success without real side effects; unknown APIs may stop execution. MIT.
records.next_check: Use a self-built PE to contrast implemented handlers, stubs, and unsupported paths.

records.name: strace
records.description: Linux system-call tracer for inspecting process I/O, signals, syscall arguments, and return values.
records.incremental_value: A practical first step for mapping process I/O before using a debugger or instrumentation framework.
records.constraints: Linux ptrace permissions and container policy affect attachment. It is syscall-level tracing. COPYING specifies LGPL-2.1-or-later for the main program, with separate test/UAPI terms.
records.next_check: Trace known file/network operations in a self-authored program and check arguments and returns.

records.name: checksec
records.description: Checks ELF security properties such as PIE, RELRO, stack canaries, and non-executable stacks; mitigation flags are not a vulnerability verdict.
records.incremental_value: A direct entry point for understanding PIE, RELRO, canaries, and NX before deeper analysis.
records.constraints: Mitigation flags are not a vulnerability verdict. Version 3.x moved from Bash to Go; the reviewed README/version text and release 3.2.0 differ. LICENSE has BSD-3-Clause-style terms.
records.next_check: Compare differently compiled ELF fixtures against independent readelf results.

records.name: wasm-tools
records.description: Bytecode Alliance tools for inspecting, validating, and transforming WebAssembly modules, components, and WIT interfaces.
records.incremental_value: Adds Component Model/WIT tasks beyond the existing WABT entry.
records.constraints: Pin the CLI or Rust library version; validation and transformation do not restore the original source. The reviewed README declares Apache-2.0, Apache-2.0 with LLVM exceptions, and MIT licensing, rather than Apache-2.0 alone.
records.next_check: Use one self-authored core module and one component/WIT fixture.

records.name: AsmResolver
records.description: Library for reading, modifying, and rebuilding native and managed PE files, including .NET metadata and application bundles.
records.incremental_value: Complements decompilers and general binary libraries with .NET metadata, application-bundle, and rebuilding APIs.
records.constraints: A developer library rather than a turnkey GUI. The v5-to-v6 migration and target-format coverage need explicit versions. MIT.
records.next_check: Modify a self-built managed PE resource/metadata field, rebuild, and verify loading.

records.name: Blutter
records.description: Flutter AOT analysis tool for recent Android arm64 libapp.so files, producing annotated assembly, object-pool dumps, and Frida templates.
records.incremental_value: Fills the missing Flutter path with annotated assembly, object-pool data, and Frida templates.
records.constraints: Currently targets recent Dart versions in Android arm64 libapp.so. It is not a general Dart source decompiler. Building requires C++20 formatting support, such as GCC 13+ or Clang 16+. MIT.
records.next_check: Pin Flutter/Dart/ABI for a self-built APK and locate a known string and function.

records.name: Renode
records.description: Embedded-system simulator with scriptable platform and peripheral models for repeatable firmware debugging and observation.
records.incremental_value: Adds repeatable board/peripheral observation and MMIO experiments beside QEMU and Linux-firmware tools.
records.constraints: ISA support does not mean every board is modeled. Correct platform descriptions and peripherals are required. Portable and non-portable host packages differ; the reviewed build/non-portable path needs .NET 6+. MIT core, separate dependency licenses.
records.next_check: Pin a supported board model, firmware, and script; compare known UART or MMIO activity.

records.name: Facedancer
records.description: Python USB device-emulation and proxy framework for compatible hardware on GNU/Linux; 3.x does not support legacy scripts and backend capabilities vary.
records.task: USB device emulation and proxy experiments
records.incremental_value: Turns protocol hypotheses into controlled device behavior rather than observation alone.
records.constraints: Requires compatible boards/backends. The reviewed README states GNU/Linux host support and no Windows support for 3.0; legacy scripts are incompatible. Endpoint, proxy, and host-mode limits vary by board. BSD-3-Clause.
records.next_check: Start with a current example on one Linux/board/backend combination and verify enumeration/endpoints.

records.name: Packetry
records.description: USB 2.0 protocol analyzer for Cynthion captures and offline PCAP files using the LINKTYPE_USB_2_0 format.
records.incremental_value: Adds a USB-bus-focused interface for Cynthion and offline captures.
records.constraints: Live capture needs Cynthion; existing LINKTYPE_USB_2_0 PCAPs can be read without the board. USB 2.0 scope, not USB 3.x. Source build requires Rust 1.93+ and GTK4. BSD-3-Clause.
records.next_check: Verify a shareable offline capture first, then record live hardware evidence separately.

records.name: Glasgow Interface Explorer
records.description: Programmable hardware interface explorer with applets for probing and interacting with digital buses; requires Glasgow hardware.
records.incremental_value: Adds applet-driven interaction with buses such as UART, SPI, I2C, JTAG, and SWD.
records.constraints: Requires Glasgow hardware and matching software/gateware/applets. Hardware capability is not a software-only feature. 0BSD.
records.next_check: Document one interface with board revision, applet, electrical setup, and observable output.

records.name: pymobiledevice3
records.description: CLI and Python API for iOS device services, including logs, crash reports, packet capture, and developer tooling with version-dependent tunnel requirements.
records.incremental_value: Adds device services such as logs, crash reports, PCAP, DVT, and WebInspector beside static ipsw and Frida workflows.
records.constraints: Python 3.9+, a pairable device, and service-specific host/iOS requirements. iOS 17+ developer services use tunnels; do not generalize this to universal jailbreak/root requirements. GPL-3.0.
records.next_check: Record one host/iOS/service combination and verify logs or WebInspector output.

records.name: Hex-Rays IDA MCP
records.description: Official IDA MCP server for agent access to binary analysis; requires IDA 9.4+ with idalib, Python 3.11+, and uv, with IDA licensing separate from the server.
records.incremental_value: An official implementation with distinct requirements beside the existing community server.
records.constraints: Requires IDA 9.4+, idalib, Python 3.11+, and uv. The MIT server license does not provide an IDA license. Official and community implementations need clear names.
records.next_check: On a licensed host, inspect a self-built binary and retain raw function/xref responses and client versions.

records.name: Chrome DevTools MCP
records.description: Official MCP server for inspecting Chrome network activity, runtime state, console output, and performance traces; requires Node.js LTS and Chrome.
records.incremental_value: Makes network, console, runtime, and performance evidence accessible through a documented agent interface.
records.constraints: Requires Node LTS and a supported Chrome installation; arbitrary Chromium forks are not proven compatible. Preserve raw responses/traces alongside interpretations. Apache-2.0.
records.next_check: Inspect a self-authored local app and retain browser/client versions and original request/console evidence.

records.name: Corkami
records.description: Visual references and posters explaining binary formats and file structures, including executable-format layouts.
records.incremental_value: Adds stable format-layout references rather than another general introductory course.
records.constraints: Reference material, not a software tool. Commit age alone does not invalidate it. Link to the author source; no image redistribution license was established by GitHub metadata.
records.next_check: Select a relevant diagram and check its format/version scope against the corresponding specification.

records.name: JEB
records.description: Android decompiler and analysis platform with edition-dependent native analysis and official MCP capabilities that vary by version; **commercial**.
records.task: Commercial Android/native analysis and official MCP
records.incremental_value: Adds a professional commercial option and its official integration as capabilities of the same product.
records.constraints: License/edition differences matter. GUI MCP predates headless CLI support; CLI MCP arrived in 5.41, and run_apk_analysis in 5.47. The reviewed changelog is 5.48. Do not describe all MCP functionality as introduced in 5.41.
records.next_check: Use an appropriate licensed edition with a self-built APK and retain versioned analysis/tool responses.

link_exceptions.evidence: Official page content retrieved during review; exact URL excluded from lychee, not the whole domain.

conditional_checks.name: hermes-dec
conditional_checks.description: Parses, disassembles, and decompiles React Native Hermes bytecode into register-based pseudo-code that is not runnable JavaScript; HBC 98 and 99 load with an unsupported-version warning.
conditional_checks.constraints: HBC 98/99 warn as not formally supported; hbc-file-parser raises TypeError on -g1 debug info; executing the pseudo-code prints 21 instead of 25 because registers are shared across functions.
conditional_checks.reproduced_scope: HBC 98/99 at -g0/-g1: header, disassembly and pseudo-code landmarks; -g1 debug-info parsing raises TypeError; executing the pseudo-code prints 21, not 25

conditional_checks.name: Malduck
conditional_checks.description: Python library of cryptography, compression, and memory-model helpers with a YARA-driven framework for writing your own malware configuration extractors; it does not ship family extractors.
conditional_checks.constraints: Extractors and YARA rules are user-supplied; useful beside FLOSS/capa, not universal family recovery.
conditional_checks.reproduced_scope: Self-authored YARA-triggered extractor and RC4 config; wrong-key and no-marker samples yield no config

conditional_checks.name: boofuzz
conditional_checks.description: Python framework for describing a protocol's message fields and sending mutated messages to a target, useful for testing a reconstructed protocol against a live service; crash detection needs a process monitor or restart callback.
conditional_checks.constraints: Replies to fuzzed messages are read only with receive_data_after_fuzz=True; String mutations are UTF-8 text and max_len counts characters; without a process monitor or restart callback a stopped target ends the run early with only an info message and no failed test case; default combinatorial depth grows quickly.
conditional_checks.reproduced_scope: Localhost TRC1 protocol: default frame, 575 payload mutations with correct length/CRC, sent and replied frames match; replies unread by default, UTF-8 string mutations, and a stopped target ends the run without a failure
